problem: Find the equation of the upward-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(-1,-4)$ and which passes through the point $(1,-2).$
worked_solution:
For any upward or downward-opening parabola with its vertex at $(h,k),$ the general standard equation is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k).
$$

Here, the vertex has coordinates $(h,k)=(-1,-4).$ Substituting these into the general standard equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-(-1))^{2} & =4p(y-(-4)) \\ (x+1)^{2} & =4p(y+4).\end{aligned}
$$

We are left to find the value of $p.$ We know that the given parabola also passes through the point $(1,-2),$ so we can substitute $x=1$ and $y=-2$ into the standard equation and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2} & =4p(y+4) \\ (1+1)^{2} & =4p(-2+4) \\ 4 & =8p \\ p & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2} & =4p(y+4) \\ (x+1)^{2} & =4(\frac{1}{2})(y+4) \\ (x+1)^{2} & =2(y+4).\end{aligned}
$$
